text:
The Trevor Zegras story in Philadelphia has turned uncomfortable. After another costly mistake, Rick Tocchet dropped him to the fourth line before the Nov. 21 game in Montreal (per several reports), and The Athletic's Kevin Kurz is fielding questions on whether Denver Barkey has replaced him at center.

The slump is stark: one goal in his last ten games, where we'd expect about seven points at his ice time, and his minutes are down almost two a night. He has gone five straight without a point. Our read is some of each. The Flyers get slightly fewer chances with him on than usual, but he still has 7.4 expected goals on his own shots against five goals, which is why we flag him as due. The team has also scored almost eight fewer goals than expected with him on the ice.

The worry is the other end. Philadelphia gets only 38% of the 5v5 expected goals with him out there, about eight points worse than without him. That is not the player Evolving-Hockey had 47th among 401 forwards last season, driving 94th-percentile chance creation. The talent hasn't vanished in a month; the results have.
headline: Trevor Zegras is getting the chances, not the results
